card: This pull request passes explicit Logger instances to Bitcoin Core kernel classes such as ChainstateManager, BlockManager, CTxMemPool, and CDBWrapper, replacing direct calls to the global logger singleton. It allows libbitcoinkernel consumers and testing harnesses to independently route, filter, and control log output rather than forcing all logging to a single process-wide destination. The change eliminates the implicitly allocated global logger in kernel code. It is based on a stack of logging PRs (#34778, #29256, #33847) and enables downstream work like contextual wallet logging in #30343.
evidence: PR description: "Pass Logger instances to BlockManager, CCoinsViewDB, CDBWrapper, Chainstate, ChainstateManager, CoinsViews, and CTxMemPool classes so libbitcoinkernel applications and tests have the option to control where log output goes instead of having all output sent to the global logger."

Commit e06a5c8737: "Current kernel logging API is too complicated and too restrictive... [the changes] allow creating a log stream, setting options on it, registering it with the btck_Context instance and receiving log messages from it."
problem: Kernel code relies on a global logger singleton, preventing libbitcoinkernel consumers and multi-instance tests from directing log output from different components to different destinations or configuring independent logging streams.
scope_notes: This PR sits on top of a multi-PR stack (#34778, #29256, and #33847) and introduces widespread mechanical changes across validation, blockstorage, mempool, and test harnesses to thread Logger references.
summary: Pass explicit Logger instances to core kernel objects including BlockManager, CCoinsViewDB, CDBWrapper, ChainstateManager, and CTxMemPool. Update internal logging in kernel code to log to these local instances instead of the global logger singleton. Remove the implicitly allocated global logger instance, requiring binaries and kernel consumers to supply or instantiate logger instances.
